title: Reverse Linked List
prompt:
A student's reading history is stored as a singly linked list, oldest book first. The app wants it newest first. Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse it in place (relink the existing nodes, don't create new ones) and return the new head.

Write reverseList(head). The helpers ListNode, fromArray and toArray are at the top of the editor; keep them, the tests use them.

  • toArray(reverseList(fromArray([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]))) gives [5, 4, 3, 2, 1]
  • reverseList(null) returns null

Constraints: 0 to 5,000 nodes. Target: O(n) time, O(1) extra space.

tests.name: single node
relinks the same nodes (in place)

hints: Trigger: "reverse a list in place" = three pointers: previous, current, next.
At each node you need to point current.next backwards to previous. But once you overwrite it, you have lost the rest of the list. So save current.next in a variable first.

Shape:

let previous = null, current = head;
while (current !== null) {
  const next = current.next;
  current.next = previous;
  previous = current;
  current = next;
}
return previous;
explain:
Time O(n): each node is visited once. Space O(1): three pointers no matter how long the list is. (A recursive version is also O(n) time but uses O(n) call-stack space.)

Say it: "I'll walk once with previous and current. At each node: save next, flip the pointer to previous, advance both. When current is null, previous is the new head. O(n) time, O(1) space."
